html: The Nyaki-nyaki were a small Aboriginal Australian group of the inland south west of Western Australia, in what is now the eastern wheatbelt. The map shows them from 1600 to 1815. Little is known about them. Their speech is said to have been a dialect either of Noongar or of Kalaamaya, the language of their neighbours to the north. Other neighbours were the Ballardong to the west and the Goreng and Wiilman to the south. Clearing for wheat farms in the early 1900s changed this country almost completely.
